body:
Not an end-user feature. Adds a new CLI verb so the load-edit-save cycle QET's undo commands drive can be exercised headlessly, for automated regression testing.

## Why

I've been building a fuzzing/regression harness this session (a Python simulator, in a separate repo, driving `--resave`). It found and I fixed two real crash/hang bugs in the XML load path this way — but most of the *other* interesting bugs in this codebase turned out not to be reachable through the existing CLI at all, because `--resave`/`--export-*`/`--info` only ever load and re-serialize. They can't delete an element, rotate a selection, or undo anything — and several real bugs (PR #664, PR #660) live specifically in what happens *during* those operations, not in load/save.

## What it adds

```
qelectrotech --test-ops <project.qet> <ops.json> <output.qet>
```

`ops.json` is a small, fixed vocabulary applied to the first diagram, through the exact same code path the GUI uses:

```json
[
  {"op": "select", "uuids": ["{...}"]},
  {"op": "delete"},
  {"op": "undo"},
  {"op": "redo"},
  {"op": "rotate", "angle": 90}
]
```

- `select` resolves uuids against the diagram's elements and selects them (unresolved uuids warn on stderr, not fatal)
- `delete` pushes `DeleteQGraphicsItemCommand` on the current selection — the same command the GUI's Delete action pushes
- `rotate` pushes `RotateSelectionCommand` — same as the GUI's plain "Pivoter"
- `undo`/`redo` step the diagram's `QUndoStack`

On completion it saves and prints one JSON line to stdout:
```json
{"ops_applied": 3, "element_count": 65, "element_info_count": 65}
```
The last two are `SELECT COUNT(*)` against the in-memory project database's `element` and `element_info` tables — directly useful for catching the PR #664 bug class (an orphan `element_info` row), independent of which operation caused it.

## Verified against a real project, not just written and hoped

Ran each op against `qet-fix/examples/741.qet`:

- **select + delete**: `element_count` drops 65→64, `element_info_count` stays 65 — reproduces PR #664 on this (unpatched) branch immediately.
- **select + delete + undo**: element restored, and stderr shows exactly the error PR #664's title names: `UNIQUE constraint failed: element_info.element_uuid`.
- **select (2 elements) + rotate**: verified with the docker repo's `simulator/canon.py` that both elements' positions and orientation changed correctly and consistently.
- **rotate + undo + redo**: round-trips to the same rotated state.
- **unknown op name**: fails cleanly, exit 2, no crash.
- **uuid that doesn't resolve**: warns on stderr, treated as an empty selection, doesn't crash.
- **`"as_group": true`**: rejected with a clear message rather than silently rotating per-item — see note below.
- Existing CLI surface (`--resave`, `--info`, `--export-*`) re-verified unaffected by the corpus-wide determinism/regression fixtures already in the docker repo.

### Cross-check against the actual PR #664 fix

To make sure this isn't just detecting *a* difference but the *right* one, I also built this against `fix-element-info-orphan-row` (your open PR #664) and ran the identical select+delete+undo sequence: `element_count` and `element_info_count` both land on 65, and the `UNIQUE constraint failed` line is gone from stderr. Same tool, same ops, opposite (correct) result depending on whether the fix is present.

## Scope notes

- **`"as_group"` rotation is intentionally not supported.** `RotateSelectionCommand` only gained that mode in PR #660, which isn't merged yet. Rather than silently falling back to per-item rotation if someone passes `as_group: true`, it's rejected outright with a message naming why — so a caller relying on it fails loudly instead of getting a quietly different result.
- I kept the vocabulary to exactly what two known, real bugs needed (delete/undo/rotate/select), not a general scripting language. There's a separate, still-undecided `SCRIPTING-RFC.md` drafted in the docker repo for broader programmatic editing — this is deliberately much smaller than that, and I don't want this PR to be read as pre-empting that decision.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
Two independent crash/hang bugs found by an adversarial mutation
harness (a simulator built this session to drive qelectrotech --resave
against corrupted/mutated real project files and check the result with
gdb rather than guess).

## 1. A single NaN/Inf coordinate hangs --resave forever

element x="nan" (or y, or on a <terminal>) survives XML parsing --
QString::toDouble(&ok) returns ok=true for "nan"/"inf"/"-inf", verified
directly -- and propagates into Conductor::shape() during diagram load.
gdb on the hung process shows 100% CPU (2.98 of 3.00s wall time was
user CPU, confirmed via /proc/<pid>/stat, not a blocked wait) stuck in:

  QPainterPathStroker::createStroke()
  <- Conductor::shape()
  <- QGraphicsItem::collidesWithItem()
  <- Conductor::calculateTextItemPosition()
  <- Diagram::addItem() <- Diagram::fromXml()

Fixed at the shared parsing point rather than in every geometry
consumer: QET::attributeIsAReal() (sources/qet.cpp), used at 26 call
sites across the codebase for exactly this "is this XML attribute a
usable real number" check, now also rejects non-finite values.
Element::valideXml() and Terminal::valideXml() previously duplicated
this parsing with their own raw toDouble(&conv_ok) -- same gap, since
conv_ok is also true for "nan" -- and now use the shared, fixed helper
instead of their own copy.

## 2. A single corrupted byte crashes the XML parser itself

QETProject::openFile() hands the raw file to
QDomDocument::setContent(QIODevice*), which does not fail cleanly on a
control character XML does not permit (the spec's Char production
allows only tab/LF/CR among bytes below 0x20) -- it segfaults inside
libQt5Xml's own DOM parser. gdb shows the crash never reaches any QET
code:

  QDomDocument::setContent(QIODevice*, ...)
  <- QETProject::openFile() <- QETProject::QETProject()

Confirmed as a class of input, not one specific byte: reproduced with
an embedded NUL (0x00, in XML whitespace), an 0x0E (also whitespace,
found by the harness's mutation sweep after the NUL fix), and an 0x19
(inside base64-encoded embedded logo data) -- identical crash address
in gdb across all three.

Fixed with a new QET::isWellFormedXmlByteStream() (sources/qet.cpp):
read the raw bytes first and refuse to hand a stream containing an
illegal control character to the parser at all, rather than try to
recover from a crash inside a library this code doesn't control.

## Verification

Both fixes verified against the original repro files (clean rejection
or clean resave instead of hang/crash) and against a clean full-corpus
resave (all 23 files in qet-fix/examples/, no new rejections -- the
byte-stream check does not false-positive on real QET output). A
150-iteration adversarial sweep with all mutators active against the
fixed build found zero crashes.

## Deliberately not fixed here

Two related gaps found during validation, listed rather than silently
folded in or silently left undocumented:

- QDomDocument::setContent() is called the same way (a QIODevice* or
  raw bytes handed straight to the parser) at roughly twenty other
  sites: sources/cli_export.cpp, sources/titleblocktemplate.cpp,
  sources/qetxml.cpp, sources/diagramview.cpp,
  sources/diagramevent/diagrameventaddmacro.cpp,
  sources/import/edz/edzpart.cpp, sources/elementtextpattern.cpp,
  sources/ElementsCollection/elementslocation.cpp,
  sources/ElementsCollection/elementstreeview.cpp,
  sources/titleblock/templateview.cpp,
  sources/editor/elementview.cpp,
  sources/editor/ui/qetelementeditor.cpp. Element/macro/title-block
  loading, EDZ import, and clipboard paste likely share the same
  crash; none of them are covered by this fix.
- A DynamicElementTextItem's position accepts and persists a non-finite
  value (confirmed: y="-inf" survives two consecutive resaves without
  crashing). Lower severity than the two bugs above -- it does not
  reach Conductor::shape() the same way an element position does, so
  it is a silent data-integrity gap rather than a hang -- and a
  different parsing path from the one this commit touches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Reject non-finite element positions and illegal XML control bytes

…sting

New CLI verb, not an end-user feature: applies a small, fixed vocabulary
of editing operations to a project's first diagram through the exact
same code path the GUI uses (DeleteQGraphicsItemCommand,
RotateSelectionCommand, QUndoStack::undo/redo), then saves. Exists to
close a gap found while building a fuzzing/regression harness this
session: most interesting bugs in this codebase are not reachable
through the existing --resave/--export-*/--info CLI, because they need
live editing -- delete, rotate, undo -- applied to an in-memory Diagram,
and the existing CLI only ever loads and re-serializes.

  qelectrotech --test-ops <project.qet> <ops.json> <output.qet>

ops.json is a JSON array of {"op": ...} objects:

  select {"uuids": [...]}   -- resolve uuids against the diagram's
                                elements and select them; unresolved
                                uuids are reported on stderr, not fatal
  delete                    -- delete the current selection
  rotate {"angle": 90}      -- rotate the current selection in place
  undo / redo                one step on the diagram's QUndoStack

On completion it prints one JSON line to stdout:
{"ops_applied": N, "element_count": N, "element_info_count": N} -- the
last two are SELECT COUNT(*) against the in-memory project database's
element and element_info tables. A mismatch between them is exactly the
orphan-row bug class PR #664 found (removeElement() never cleaning
element_info), independent of which operation caused it -- checking the
row counts directly is more robust than trying to detect the resulting
UNIQUE-constraint failure by scraping stderr.

"as_group" rotation (rotate the selection as one rigid body) is
deliberately NOT supported here: RotateSelectionCommand only grew that
mode in PR #660, not merged as of this writing. An "as_group" key is
rejected with a clear message rather than silently falling back to
per-item rotation, so a caller relying on it fails loudly instead of
getting a different result than asked for.

Verified against a real project (qet-fix/examples/741.qet), not just
by inspection:

  - select + delete: element_count drops 65->64, element_info_count
    stays 65 -- reproduces PR #664 on an unpatched build immediately.
  - select + delete + undo: element restored (element_count back to
    65), and stderr shows the exact error PR #664's title describes:
    "UNIQUE constraint failed: element_info.element_uuid".
  - select (2 elements) + rotate: verified via the docker repo's
    simulator/canon.py that both elements' positions and orientation
    changed correctly and consistently.
  - rotate + undo + redo: round-trips to the same rotated state.
  - unknown op name: fails cleanly, exit 2, no crash.
  - uuid that does not resolve: warns on stderr, treated as an empty
    selection, does not crash.
  - "as_group": true on this (pre-#660) build: rejected with a clear
    message, exit 2, rather than silently rotating per-item.

Full existing CLI surface (--resave, --info, --export-*) re-verified
unaffected: fixture_determinism.py and fixture_known_bugs.py (docker
repo's simulator/) both still report their expected results against
this build.
